question.text: What is folio consolidation in mutual funds?

answer.text: Merging multiple folios of the same investor under the same AMC into a single folio
Merging folios of different investors who are family members
Converting physical folios to demat form
Combining folios across different AMCs into a single folio

explanation.text: The Logic: Folio consolidation refers to merging multiple folios of the same investor (same PAN, same holding pattern) held within the same AMC into a single folio. This simplifies portfolio tracking, reduces duplicate statements, and unifies tax computation. Folios across different AMCs cannot be combined into a single folio — each AMC maintains its own folio register; the Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) provides cross-AMC consolidation for viewing only, not at the folio level. The Trap: Option B mistakenly extends consolidation to different investors. Option C confuses consolidation with dematerialisation. Option D conflates folio-level merging with CAS-level cross-AMC reporting. Note: The cited NISM Series II-B workbook pages define folios and account/CAS consolidation, but do not specifically define folio consolidation as merging multiple folios of the same investor under one AMC into a single folio. The framing above reflects general RTA industry practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
